rounds.text: Tarmat Ltd trades at a highly attractive price-to-book ratio of 0.71x against a book value of ₹ 76.2 [E2], and also sits well below the sector benchmark P/B of 1.19x [E7]. Fundamental momentum has broken out forcefully in the trailing periods, highlighted by a 28% compounded sales growth [E17], a massive 175% compounded profit growth [E21], and screen metrics showing recent sales surging 65% YoY alongside net profit jumping 92% YoY [E67, E69]. This earnings acceleration is underpinned by structural margin expansion, with operating margins climbing to 7% in the TTM from 3% three years prior [E30] and reaching 9% in the most recent September quarter [E31], supported by an increasing yearly operating-margin trend over the last five years [E32]. Furthermore, profits are backed by strong cash conversion of 1.33x with ₹ 8 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026 [E34, E35], all operating against a supportive construction sector tailwind score of +0.55 [E77]. Conceded: long-term historical sales growth has been weak, reflected in a 10-year compounded rate of 3% [E14] and a 5-year rate of -10% [E15], alongside low multi-year returns on equity [E26, E27].

Tarmat Ltd carries a valuation that is fundamentally unsupported by its intrinsic worth, evidenced by a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 38 per share against a market price of Rs 54, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -42.1% [E44, E45]. Furthermore, the stock's reverse DCF reveals that the current price already demands an aggressive 5.8% earnings growth, while the base case assumes a meager 1.0% [E46]. This rich pricing is paired with an exceptionally weak historical performance, marked by a 5-year compounded sales growth of -10% and a 3-year compounded sales growth of -7% [E15, E16]. Profitability metrics are equally concerning, with a trailing return on equity of 3.0% and a 10-year median ROE of just 1% [E13, E26]. Compounded share price growth over the past 3 and 5 years reflects this stagnation at -13% and -3% respectively, while annualised volatility remains high at 63.6% alongside a dismal Sharpe ratio of 0.16 [E23, E24, E53, E54]. Conceded: operating margins are increasing over the last 5 years and trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 175% [E21, E32].

Conceded: [E44], [E45], and [E46]. However, the bear's reliance on backward-looking historical averages completely ignores an inflection point in operational momentum, highlighted by trailing twelve-month profit growth of 175% and sales growth of 28% [E17, E21]. The bear dismisses valuation context by ignoring that the stock trades at a significant discount to book value at 0.71x, alongside a price-to-book ratio lower than the sector benchmark [E2, E7]. Furthermore, the bear's historical critique of margins is countered by a continuous, multi-year expansion, with operating margins rising across the last five years and expanding by 4 percentage points in the trailing twelve months and latest quarter [E30, E31, E32, E33]. Financial health is robustly underpinned by conservative financing with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.11x and strong cash conversion of 1.33x where profits are fully backed by operational cash [E34, E37]. Finally, the business operates within a supportive construction sector tailwind with a positive tailwind score of +0.55, directly aiding its recent outperformance [E75, E77].

Conceded: [E17], [E21], [E30], [E31], [E32], [E33], [E34], [E37], [E75], and [E77]. While the bull points to these positive operational indicators, they obscure a deeply rooted multi-year structural decline in top-line performance, evidenced by a 5-year compounded sales growth of -10% and a 3-year compounded sales growth of -7% [E15, E16]. The bull highlights a low price-to-book ratio of 0.71x [E2], but ignores that this depressed valuation is entirely justified by a multi-year record of dismal capital efficiency, featuring a 3-year median return on equity of just 2% [E28] and an annualised ROCE of only 3.4% [E12]. Furthermore, the bull overlooks severe intrinsic valuation risk where a discounted cash flow model values the stock at Rs 38 against a market price of Rs 54, yielding a negative margin of safety of -42.1% [E44, E45]. Finally, low promoter ownership at 29.11%, which has declined by 4.14 percentage points over recent years, combined with a total absence of dividend payouts, demonstrates a lack of insider conviction that directly undermines the bull's growth narrative [E41, E60, E62].
